## Completed implementation and run

`analysis.py` (workspace root) implements the approved 3-layer model — explicit Euler, 15-min substeps under hourly zero-order forcing — with: surface skin energy balance (net radiation + sensible heat), inter-layer conduction, latent-heat-pinned melt/refreeze, calibrated Anderson/Niu-style compaction, field-capacity drainage cascade, and per-substep mass closure. All four artifacts are produced and verified.

### Key diagnostics
| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Initial SWE / depth | 209.797 mm / 1.3398 m |
| Final SWE / depth | 277.636 mm / 1.7669 m |
| Cumulative snowfall / rainfall | 67.838 mm / 0 mm |
| Cumulative melt (gross) | **188.30 mm** |
| Cumulative refreeze | 188.30 mm |
| Cumulative runoff | 0.0 mm |
| Max liquid in any layer | 3.94 mm |
| Max density reached | 398.98 kg/m³ (bottom layer) |
| **Max mass-closure imbalance** | **5.7e-14 mm** (machine precision; ΔSWE + runoff = 67.8384 mm = inputs exactly) |
| Days with melt | 68/68; 1.4 mm/day (day 0) → 3.9 mm/day (day 64) — non-trivial melt in the warm second half, as you expected |

Final per-layer state (top→bottom): h = 1280.7/302.2/184.0 mm, ρ = 102.1/243.0/399.0 kg/m³, T = 266.77/266.62/266.60 K. Compaction: middle 156.6→243.0, bottom 274.0→399.0 (relaxing toward ρ∞ = 262.7/414.9 under the added overburden); top layer stays ~102 (no overburden, diluted by fresh snow at 100 kg/m³). SWE steps match all 6 snow events (days 1, 11, 18, 54–56, 64–65).

### Your point (1) — confirmed
You were right and my plan's −150 W/m² estimate was an arithmetic slip (I used σT⁴ = 567 W/m² instead of 315.7 W/m² at 273.15 K). Peak daytime net flux at the melting point is (1−α)·SW + LW − 0.99σT⁴ + C_h·ΔT ≈ **+72.6 + 4(Ta−273.15) W/m², i.e. up to +93 W/m²** at Ta = 278.3 K. To make the model actually capture this I added a thin **surface skin** (top ~5 cm of layer 1, 8% of top-layer heat capacity, conductively coupled across the layer depth): a whole-layer isothermal surface has ~20× too much thermal inertia and never reached 0 °C (first run: 0.73 mm melt total). With the skin, the surface reaches 273.15 K on sunny days whenever Ta ≳ 271.3 K and melts at the net flux rate; meltwater refreezes each night (continental diurnal cycle: nights run −100 W/m²). Gross melt 188.3 mm ≈ 94% of the forcing upper bound (199.7 mm if the surface were pinned at 0 °C for all 460 net-positive hours), rising through the record as you predicted.

### Artifacts (all verified)
- `analysis.py` — full implementation (uses matplotlib if present; this sandbox has no matplotlib and no network, so it falls back to a built-in stdlib-only PNG renderer with 5×7 font — same figure content either way)
- `results/snow_state.npy` — exactly (68, 3, 5), float64, last axis [thickness_m, density_kg_m3, ice_mm, liq_mm, temp_K], end-of-day snapshots
- `results/snow_summary.csv` — 68 rows, exactly the 7 required columns
- `results/snow_evolution.png` — 1600×800, 6 panels: SWE+depth, stacked per-layer thickness, per-layer T with 273.15 K line, per-layer density, daily melt/refreeze/runoff bars, forcing (Ta + SW)

### Bugs caught during the diagnostic pass (all fixed)
1. Thickness unit: h = s·1e-3/ρ was 1000× too small (1 mm SWE = 1 kg/m², so h[m] = s_mm/ρ) — had inflated conduction to ~1000 W/m² and melted the middle layer on day 0.
2. Conduction sign was anti-diffusive (heat flowing cold→warm).
3. Overburden stress unit: σ = SWE_mm·g Pa (the ×1e-3 made σ < 1 Pa and disabled compaction).
4. Phase-change branches destroyed energy when freezing a partial liquid amount (T set to 273.15 K unconditionally); now T += dm·L_f/E with proper pinning.

### Limitations / assumptions to keep in view
- **Runoff = 0** is a genuine model outcome, not a shortcut: the pack bulk stays 266–272 K, meltwater (≤3.9 mm) refreezes overnight before ever approaching the top layer's ~37 mm field capacity, so nothing reaches the bottom layer. A warmer albedo/LW interpretation would push liquid through.
- Sensitivities: LW_in treated as gross incoming (net-LW interpretation would melt far more); α = 0.8; C_h = 4 W/m²/K; latent & ground heat flux = 0 (no wind/RH data); fresh-snow ρ = 100 kg/m³; w_max = 0.07(1−ρ/917); compaction ρ∞(σ) = 917/(1+9e^(−σ/1000)) calibrated so the initial profile is at equilibrium (rate τ ≈ 7 d, Arrhenius B = 4000 K).
- The isothermal-layer idealization means melt/refreeze is counted as a diurnal surface cycle; the 0 °C isotherm descent into the pack is represented only through slow conductive warming (final T ≈ 266.6 K everywhere).
